title: India Take on West Indies in Lucknow as T20I Series Begins Tuesday
excerpt: The first of five T20Is starts at 7 p.m. IST on October 6 at Lucknow's Ekana Stadium, with Shreyas Iyer leading a young Indian side against Shai Hope's West Indies. Star Sports and JioHotstar carry the game in India; Willow TV streams it in the US.
body:
• First T20I: India vs West Indies on Tuesday, October 6, at 7:00 p.m. IST (toss at 6:30 p.m.) at the Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium, Lucknow. Five-match series runs to October 17.
  • Shreyas Iyer captains India with Tilak Varma as vice-captain; the squad blends experience with youth, including teenage prospect Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Shai Hope leads the West Indies.
  • Head-to-head in T20Is: 31 meetings — 20 wins for India, 10 for the West Indies, one no-result.
  • How to watch: in India, Star Sports Network telecasts the match and JioHotstar streams it live. In the US and Canada, Willow TV streams it at 9:30 a.m. ET / 6:30 a.m. PT (Willow TV lists $9.99/month, no free trial); in the UK, Sky Sports Cricket airs it at 2:30 p.m. BST.

India begin a five-match T20I series against the West Indies on Tuesday evening, with the first game starting at 7:00 p.m. IST at the Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium in Lucknow. The toss is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. The series, which also stops in Ranchi, Indore, Hyderabad and Bengaluru before concluding on October 17, is the first time Shreyas Iyer leads India in the T20I format.

A new-look India after the ODI leg

The West Indies tour opened with a three-match ODI leg from September 27 to October 3, for which India fielded a star-heavy squad led by Shubman Gill and featuring Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul as vice-captain. The T20I setup is deliberately different: a younger group built around the next generation of India's short-format batting.

Shreyas Iyer takes charge of the T20I side with Tilak Varma as his deputy. The squad includes Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan and Sanju Samson as the wicketkeepers, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Axar Patel among the allrounders, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav and Ravi Bishnoi in the spin department, and Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav and Mayank Yadav as the pace options, according to the squad lists published across Indian sports media.

The West Indies, captained by wicketkeeper-batter Shai Hope, have brought a squad full of T20 specialists: Roston Chase, Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Romario Shepherd, Matthew Forde, Shamar Joseph, Akeal Hosein, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul, Kamil Pooran, Jewel Andrew, Quentin Sampson and Shamar Springer. It is the format where the Caribbean side has historically punched closest to its weight against India.

Players to watch

Abhishek Sharma: India's most destructive T20 opener right now; the pace at which he attacks powerplays has made him the batter West Indies must account for first. Shreyas Iyer: his first series as T20I captain will be judged on selection calls and tempo management as much as runs. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: the teenage prodigy gets a senior-stage audition on home turf. Arshdeep Singh: India's designated death-overs leader, tasked with closing out innings on a Lucknow surface expected to slow down. Kuldeep Yadav: his wrist-spin through the middle overs has been India's difference-maker in recent home series.

For the visitors: Shai Hope: the calm at the top of the order and a captain who reads conditions well; Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell and Sherfane Rutherford: a middle order built to clear big boundaries late; Romario Shepherd: a seam-bowling allrounder who gives balance; and Shamar Joseph: raw pace that has unsettled top orders before.

Head-to-head and what's at stake

The two sides have met 31 times in T20Is: India have won 20, the West Indies 10, with one no-result. The most recent meeting came at the T20 World Cup 2026 in March, when India hosted the Super 8s. This series is less about the trophy and more about auditions — India are using it to test young combinations ahead of a packed international calendar, while the West Indies, locked out of automatic qualification for the next global tournament, need every bilateral win to build momentum.

Series schedule and how to watch

All five T20Is begin at 7:00 p.m. IST: October 6 in Lucknow, October 9 in Ranchi, October 11 in Indore, October 14 in Hyderabad and October 17 in Bengaluru. That start time works out to 9:30 a.m. ET / 6:30 a.m. PT in the US, 2:30 p.m. BST in the UK and 5:30 p.m. GST in the UAE.

Broadcasters, per Wisden and cricket media listings: India — Star Sports Network on TV, JioHotstar streaming (a subscription plan is required). US and Canada — Willow TV, the 24/7 cricket channel available via cable, satellite and streaming. UK and Ireland — Sky Sports Cricket, with Sky Go and NOW. West Indies — ESPN Caribbean. Pakistan — Tapmad streaming. Australia — Fox Cricket and Kayo. India fans also have a free option: DD Sports carries the series on DD Free Dish DTH.

What to watch for

How Iyer balances two wicketkeepers in one XI, whether Sooryavanshi gets a debut in the series opener, and whether India's young pace attack of Arshdeep, Prince Yadav and Mayank Yadav can hold up at the death. For the West Indies, the question is whether their power-hitting depth can chase on slowing Indian pitches — Ranchi and Lucknow in particular reward spinners. Expect India to rotate; with five games in 12 days, managing workloads matters as much as winning each night.
